import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2
HID = 24


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * HID, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.type_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        h = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.type_mix, self.type_out):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            z = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(out(z).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

C3 = 16
WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        Z = int(spec.Z)
        self.Z = Z
        self.c3a = nn.Conv3d(8, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.c3b = nn.Conv3d(C3, C3, 3, padding=1)
        self.fuse = nn.Conv2d(C3 * Z, WIDTH, 1)
        if Z > 1:
            zc = torch.linspace(0.0, 1.0, Z)
        else:
            zc = torch.zeros(1)
        self.register_buffer('zpos', zc.view(1, 1, Z, 1, 1))
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zp = self.zpos.expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, planes, zp], dim=1)
        h = F.relu(self.c3a(x))
        h = F.relu(self.c3b(h))
        f = F.relu(self.fuse(h.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HEADS = 4


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W = WIDTH
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.conv = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        self.pos = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, int(spec.Y) * int(spec.X), W))
        nn.init.normal_(self.pos, std=0.02)
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(W)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(W, 3 * W)
        self.proj = nn.Linear(W, W)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(W)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(W, 2 * W), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(2 * W, W))
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(W, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(W, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(W, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = F.relu(self.stem(obs))
        f = F.relu(f + self.conv(f))
        B, C, Y, X = f.shape
        N = Y * X
        D = C // HEADS
        t = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2) + self.pos
        h = self.ln1(t)
        qkv = self.qkv(h).reshape(B, N, 3, HEADS, D).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q, k, v = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(D), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, C)
        t = t + self.proj(o)
        t = t + self.mlp(self.ln2(t))
        f = t.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, Y, X)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 48
HID = 24
BLOCKS = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.stem = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.convs = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * HID, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.type_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

        g0 = self.bcast(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(f + g0[:, :, None, None])

        outs = []

            z = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))

        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)

        self.type_mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * HID, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.type_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        vox = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X)
        planes = obs[:, 4 * Z:4 * Z + 3].unsqueeze(2).expand(B, 3, Z, Y, X)
        zp = self.zpos.expand(B, 1, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([vox, planes, zp], dim=1)
        h3 = F.relu(self.c3a(x))
        h3 = F.relu(self.c3b(h3))
        f = F.relu(self.fuse(h3.reshape(B, C3 * Z, Y, X)))
        g0 = self.bcast(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(f + g0[:, :, None, None])
        h = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, out in zip(self.fps, self.type_mix, self.type_out):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            z = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)))
            outs.append(out(z).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.name: footprint head + learned footprint conv
trials.hypothesis: Same as r2c1, except each brick type also gets a learned convolution whose kernel is exactly its footprint (dy by dx), added to the mix of max/min/mean pools before the ReLU. The fixed pools give order statistics; the learned kernel can tell cell positions apart inside the footprint (for example, a 2x2 brick overhanging one column). The cost is about 1.3x. Refuted if it scores at or below r2c1.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
HID = 24


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.bcast = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.cell = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, HID, 1)
        self.type_mix = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(3 * HID, HID, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.type_fconv = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, HID, (dy, dx), bias=False) for (dy, dx) in self.fps])
        self.type_out = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(HID, 1, 1) for _ in self.fps])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = F.relu(self.conv1(obs))
        g0 = self.bcast(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = F.relu(f + g0[:, :, None, None])
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(f))
        h = self.cell(f)
        outs = []
        for (dy, dx), mix, fc, out in zip(self.fps, self.type_mix, self.type_fconv, self.type_out):
            hp = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(hp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            z = F.relu(mix(torch.cat([mx, mn, av], dim=1)) + fc(hp))
            outs.append(out(z).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no results yet, so these candidates rest on the structure of the task and the budget rule. Bigger networks train on fewer steps, so all three stay close to the starting network's compute (about 1.1 to 1.45 times). The starting network's placement head reads features at one anchor cell only. But a brick's outcome depends on its whole footprint: it lands one layer above the highest cell under it, and it is correct only if every cell it fills is missing from the build. That points to three tests: (A) a head that pools learned features over each brick's footprint, (B) a deeper residual body with global context, which helps ordering and DONE decisions, and (C) a 3D voxel encoder that treats layers alike, matching the drop rule. Scores are hidden, so the only feedback will be whether each trial trains cleanly. Results from later rounds are only meaningful against the 2-seed noise.
analyses.2: No scores are visible, so round 1 tells us only that all three ideas trained within the limits. Footprint pooling cost 1.18x compute, the residual body with global broadcast 1.5x (about 87k steps), and the voxel encoder 1.12x. Without scores, the best use of the remaining trials is to build several distinct candidates that are cheap enough to keep their training steps. The end-of-search selection will pick among them by real dev score. The task has two non-local parts. The agent must see the whole design to choose a safe build order and when to choose DONE, and it must know which placements land at the right height. So this round tests: (1) combining the footprint-pooled head with global context, (2) feeding the legal-action mask in as input, since it tells the network about height limits, and (3) one light self-attention layer over the cells, which gives every cell global reach at about the starting compute.
analyses.3: Scores are hidden, so I can only reason from the task structure and from the fact that all six trials ran without errors. Each trial cost 1.04 to 1.5 times the starting compute. To place a brick correctly, the agent needs its landing height, which is the maximum build height under the footprint. It also needs to know whether every covered cell at that layer is missing, and whether the brick would seal an unbuilt target cell beneath an overhang. These are per-column, per-footprint functions, which suits footprint pooling (r1c1, r2c1). Global context (r1c2, r2c1, r2c2) mainly helps with ordering and with choosing DONE. The final selection rewards the best real score, so I'll spread bets across plausible strong designs: two refinements of r2c1, the most task-shaped design so far, and one new idea. The new idea is a per-column nonlinear stem, which tests whether the column-height reasoning is the bottleneck. I keep every cost near 1.2x so the step budget stays high.
